title: Stxbp1 loss drives different presynaptic stress outputs in L4/5 IT, MB Glut, and Pvalb neurons
exact_observed_result: Stxbp1 was lower in all 22 measured Stxbp1 cell types and reached target-row FDR in 10. L4/5 IT cells carried the largest non-target signature, 155 MB Glut had a smaller stress/adhesion program, and Pvalb GABA cells reduced Slc6a1 while direct Slc6a1 knockdown remained target-only.
biological_interpretation: Munc18-1 depletion is a privileged presynaptic perturbation that can be seen by scRNA-seq, but the transcriptional consequences split by neuronal class and are not reproduced by every SNARE or vesicle-fusion gene.

support.description: L4/5 IT cortical glutamatergic cells showed target depletion plus broad synaptic down-regulation and a neurosecretory counter-module.
MB Glut and Pvalb used different marker sets, and Snap25 had fewer non-target hits in matched classes.

caveats: Several Stxbp1-engaged classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, had no non-target 5% FDR hit.
Snap25 and Stx1b were used only as non-interchangeability comparators, not as members of the Stxbp1 transcriptional state.
The assay reads steady-state cell-body RNA and misses acute vesicle-fusion physiology.

prior_expectation.summary: STXBP1/Munc18-1 is a syntaxin-binding Sec1/Munc18 factor in neurotransmitter release; loss of STXBP1 is expected to affect synaptic biology, but the report-level evidence shows that acute mRNA remodeling is much more specific than generic SNARE membership.
